claim.why_it_matters: Printed as a numbered section heading; the markdown has it as a plain paragraph with no heading marker. A heading missing or at the wrong level breaks the section structure that navigation and clause lookup by section number rely on; the wording itself is intact.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (IV-13) shows '4.3.1.2 Conceptual Characteristics of a File' as a numbered heading in the same plain body type as 4.3, 4.3.1 and 4.3.1.1. The markdown (page-159.md line 21) carries the identical text, on its own line, at the right position, with the section number intact, so a lookup by section number still finds it. The transcription renders EVERY heading on this page (4.3, 4.3.1, 4.3.1.1, 4.3.1.2) as a plain paragraph with no '#' marker; this is the transcription's uniform formatting convention for the page, not a missing or misplaced heading. The claim itself concedes the wording is intact. The difference is formatting only and changes no content or meaning.
